free_tier.stated: 1 TiB of Volume storage free per workspace on the Starter plan ('Volumes include up to 1 TiB free'; 'Volumes $0.09 / GiB / mo *includes 1 TiB / mo free'), plus 1 TiB/month free network egress. This is the single largest clean free-tier number found in this slot.

retention.stated: Files must be < 1 TiB each; Volumes v1 capped at 500,000 inodes (v2 removes the inode cap); concurrent commits should stay under ~5; billing is a daily snapshot of total storage and deletions keep billing for up to 4 days.

egress.terms: 1 TiB/month free egress on Starter (10 TiB on Team, 100 TiB on Enterprise); beyond that $0.04/GiB. Not CDN'd for public download — egress is measured per workspace.

tooling: modal Python SDK (`modal.Volume`, `modal volume put/get/ls` CLI), a real distributed POSIX-ish filesystem mounted into containers, 25 MB chunking + caching. Not S3, and no public HTTP object URL — you must go through the CLI or a small deployed app. Frontend download UI caps at 16 MB/file, so bulk extraction is CLI-only.
chaining: 1 TiB x unlimited free workspaces (each a separate account/org with its own Starter plan). Also separate storage objects: multiple Volumes per workspace, and Volumes are independent of the $30/month compute credit — the 1 TiB is a storage allowance, not compute spend, so idling costs nothing.
limits_note: Files must be < 1 TiB each; Volumes v1 capped at 500,000 inodes (v2 removes the inode cap); concurrent commits should stay under ~5; billing is a daily snapshot of total storage and deletions keep billing for up to 4 days.
reliability_note: Very stable; the awkward part is retrieval latency and the absence of a public URL — this is storage you must front with your own service, so it fits the 'cold archive' workload better than 'serving'.

evidence.proved: 'Volumes $0.09 / GiB / mo *includes 1 TiB / mo free'; FAQ: 'Included usage applies to compute ... Volumes include up to 1 TiB free.'; plan table 'Included network egress 1 TiB / month' (Starter)
